mutants.reason: With && a WRAP read is rejected only if both length and alignment are bad, so a WRAP read with an illegal length (not 2/4/8/16 beats) or a misaligned start is accepted and goes to APB instead of returning SLVERR.

The AW context (ID, address, len, size, burst, prot, beat count, err) is captured only when the write FSM is not IDLE, so it is never captured on the AW handshake; BID, address and beat count are wrong.
The default for WREADY becomes 1, so WREADY is high in every state, including before AW is accepted and during APB and B phases. W beats are accepted early or dropped.
The write FSM leaves REQ only when the APB controller is not ready, so the request handshake is inverted. The write stalls or advances at the wrong time and APB writes are lost or hang.
The WRAP wrap-detect comparison is inverted, so the next write beat address is wrong. It does not wrap at the boundary and wraps where it should not.
The request ready to the sequencers is raised only when the APB FSM is not IDLE, so the payload is accepted at the wrong time. The sequencer handshake is wrong and transfers are lost or hang.
The response (PRDATA and PSLVERR) is captured when the APB FSM is not in ACCESS and PREADY=1, not at the completion edge. Read data and error status are wrong and the response valid is mistimed.

Precedence turns the write-error set into (WAIT && rsp_valid) || rsp_err. The registered write response error stays 1 after an erroring write, so the next write has its error flag forced to 1 and returns SLVERR wrongly.

Line 165 is only the default assignment of o_apb_pwrite in the combinational block. Every branch of the following case (SETUP, ACCESS and default) reassigns o_apb_pwrite, so the default is always overwritten and no output changes.
The default of w_ar_valid becomes 0 and later code only clears it, so every read is judged unsupported. Legal reads return SLVERR with no APB access.
Write requests are captured with the direction flag 0, so PWRITE is low for writes and the APB write becomes a read. The write response path is not triggered.
The default for ARREADY becomes 1, so ARREADY is high in all states regardless of grant. An AR is accepted while another transaction is active, or the handshake is spurious.
WDAT and DRAIN cannot both be true, so WREADY is never raised. W beats are never accepted, and the write and drain of unsupported writes hang.

reg_turn_rd is read only in the arbiter IDLE state. i_rd_done can only occur while the controller is in ACTRD, and the exit ACTRD to IDLE happens on i_rd_done, which also sets turn_rd=0 in the original. The mutant only sets turn_rd=0 earlier, while in ACTRD, where it is unobservable. Reset has priority, so no port behaviour differs.
gnt_rd and gnt_wr are mutually exclusive, so the AND of both terms is never true. The APB FSM never leaves IDLE and no APB transfer is ever issued.
The 4-KiB crossing flag is inverted: crossing reads are accepted and non-crossing reads are rejected as unsupported.
RVALID and RLAST are asserted in all states except RESP (including IDLE, REQ and WAIT) and not in RESP. R beats appear at the wrong time, and RLAST is mistimed.

RDATA is forced to 0 with SLVERR in every state except ERR. Good read data is replaced by zero SLVERR, and error beats in ERR state keep register data and resp, so SLVERR/zero data is no longer guaranteed.
With || the beat counter and address advance in RESP/ERR even when RREADY=0, and also in other states when RREADY=1. The beat count, RLAST and held payload under RREADY backpressure break.
The write-done to the arbiter is stuck at 0, so the owner is never released after the B handshake. The bridge hangs after the first write and the tie preference never flips.
RESP and ERR cannot both hold, so RVALID and RLAST are never asserted. No R beats are returned and the read hangs.
The write request valid is asserted in every state except REQ, so the request handshake is mistimed. The APB write is issued at the wrong time or never, and unsupported writes issue APB requests.
The default for AWREADY becomes 1, so AWREADY is high in every state. An AW handshake can occur while another transaction owns the bridge, and AW is accepted without the grant.
The write FSM leaves WAIT when no APB response is valid, instead of when it is. It does not wait for APB completion, so beats and B are issued before the APB write completes.
The WRAP alignment check is inverted, so aligned legal WRAP writes are rejected as unsupported (SLVERR with no APB) and misaligned ones are accepted.
The tie preference is inverted, so AW wins the first tie after reset and the later alternation is also reversed. This breaks the AR-first and flip rules.

The payload (address, direction, data, strobe, prot) is captured only when the APB FSM is not IDLE, but the ready used in the same condition is high only in IDLE. The capture never happens and APB transfers carry zero payload.

With || the write data and strobe are latched, and the beat counter is decremented, whenever WVALID is high in any state. WVALID before AW or during an APB wait corrupts the held PWDATA/PSTRB and the beat count.
In the IDLE/default branch PENABLE is driven 1 while PSEL=0, so PENABLE=1 without PSEL and APB setup/idle protocol is violated.
For ARLEN=7 (8-beat WRAP) the length is marked invalid, so legal 8-beat WRAP reads are rejected with SLVERR and no APB access.
PSEL is 0 in the ACCESS phase while PENABLE=1, so the APB access phase is not selected. The transfer protocol and the hold during wait states are violated.
The beat count has an extra 256 added, so the INCR total bytes for the 4-KiB check are far too large. Legal INCR reads near a page end are rejected as crossing 4 KiB.
With && a WRAP write is rejected only if both length and alignment are bad, so illegal-length or misaligned WRAP writes are accepted and performed on APB instead of being drained with SLVERR.

With o_gnt_rd || i_rd_req_valid the APB FSM leaves IDLE whenever the read is granted, even with no request valid. An unsupported read (ERR state) or the gap between beats starts a spurious APB transfer.
The WRAP next-address comparison is inverted for reads, so the beat address does not wrap at the boundary and wraps where it should not.
RLAST is asserted on every beat except the last, so it is high on non-final beats and low on the final one.
